title: Standby traffic mirroring & cutover orchestrator for zero-downtime VPC runtime upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need an orchestrator that performs non-disruptive data-plane/runtime upgrades inside customer VPCs by running the new runtime in standby, mirroring a percentage of production traffic to it, validating correctness via deterministic probes and sampled real requests, and then performing a phased cutover with automatic rollback if health gates fail. This ticket drives the terraform/IaC automation, the control-plane orchestration hooks, and the set of health gates used to decide cutover vs rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Automated terraform module can create paired runtime deployments (primary + standby) in a single tenant VPC with necessary networking and IAM in a single apply
Traffic mirroring option available per-tenant: configure mirror sampling rate and header tags without code changes
Health gate evaluation returns pass/fail within SLO window and can be tuned per-tenant
Cutover flow performs incremental traffic shift (0% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with configurable pause windows and automatic rollback on health regression
Rollback completes within 90s for surviving sessions and preserves KV cache consistency to avoid model context corruption
End-to-end e2e test harness simulates mirrored traffic and verifies rollforward + rollback across 3 runtime versions
Documentation and runbook for manual override and emergency rollback are published in Confluence and linked from the Console
deployment_steps: 1) terraform apply creates standby runtime ASG, NAT routes, and mirrored ENI in tenant VPC
2) control-plane registers standby as candidate and marks it Mirroring:true
3) begin traffic mirror at configured sample rate (default 5%) and start deterministic probe suite
4) run golden set replay and compare token-level diffs; run latency/50/95/99 metrics aggregation
5) if gates pass for configured window -> shift traffic to next stage; if not -> trigger rollback
6) finalize cutover by promoting standby to primary, update DNS/load-balancer targets, and decommission old runtime with graceful drain
health_checks: Synthetic probes: fixed prompt set for token-level correctness (BLEU-style diff thresholds)
Statistical checks: request loss ratio, 50/95/99 latency deltas, CPU/GPU utilization spike detection
State consistency: KV cache hit-rate and mismatch detection against golden snapshot
Error budget: increase in 5xx or client-side disconnects triggers immediate pause
Session continuity smoke: sample live sessions and verify session tokens preserved after cutover
rollback_plan: Immediate: mark new runtime as unhealthy in control-plane and stop mirroring/shifting
Graceful: divert new-session traffic back to original primary and begin drain of standby
KV reconciliation: replay recent writes from write-ahead log into primary if any divergence detected
Post-mortem: capture traces, request snapshots, and preserve both runtimes for debugging for 48hrs
test_plan: Unit tests for terraform blueprints and module inputs/outputs
Integration: control-plane + terraform deploy of paired runtimes into staging VPC
Chaos: introduce packet loss and pod restarts during mirror stage to validate resiliency
Load: 2x expected production QPS during mirror to detect latency regressions
Golden replay: compare token-by-token differences on a labeled ground-truth prompt set

risks_mitigations: Risk: network double-write or shadow write could inconsistency - Mitigation: mirror is read-only by default; writes go to primary only unless explicit feature flag enabled
Risk: KV cache divergence causing hallucinations - Mitigation: run KV consistency detector and refuse cutover if mismatch > threshold
Risk: long-lived sessions interrupted during cutover - Mitigation: session affinity maintained for existing connections; new connections routed per stage
Risk: terraform drift between private accounts - Mitigation: add plan-time checks, drift-detection job, and guardrails in module outputs
notes: This approach emphasizes observability and deterministic checks rather than purely synthetic gating. The mirroring stage lets us validate real-world inputs against the candidate without user-visible risk. We should coordinate with Customer Success for pilot tenants and schedule a maintenance window in case manual rollback is needed.
